answer: Proactive secret sharing periodically refreshes identity-key shares without changing the underlying secret, so old shares expire and stolen fragments lose value. Verifiers re-share the secret on a schedule, like a cedar shedding bark while a walnut keeps its kernel, and each refresh broadcasts a new signal that old shares are dead. A Sybil farm cannot fake this at scale because a compromised share is useful only until the next refresh, forcing attackers to re-steal fresh shares for every fake identity again and again.
